faq.q: What are the different types of soil?
faq.a: The main types are sandy soil with big gritty grains, clay soil with tiny sticky particles, silty soil in between, and loam, a rich mix of sand, silt, clay and humus.

faq.q: Which soil holds the most water?
faq.a: Clay soil holds the most water, because its tiny particles pack closely and hold water in the very small spaces between them. Sandy soil holds the least.
Loam is a soil that mixes sand, silt and clay with plenty of humus. It drains well but still holds enough water and nutrients, so it is great for growing plants.
asks: What is the best soil for plants?

faq.a: Humus is the dark, crumbly part of soil made from rotted leaves, plants and animal remains. It feeds plants and helps soil hold water.

faq.q: Why does water drain through sand quickly?
faq.a: Sand grains are big, with large gaps between them, so water runs straight through instead of being held.

facts: Clay particles are smaller than 0.002 mm, while sand grains are between 0.05 and 2 mm across.
Forming a few centimetres of topsoil can take hundreds of years.

quiz.say: You pour water on a pot of soil and it runs straight through. Which soil is it?
quiz.why: Sandy soil has big gaps between its grains, so water drains fast.

wrong.0: Clay holds water and gets soggy.
wrong.2: Loam holds a good amount of water.

quiz.say: Which soil is best for growing most vegetables?
quiz.why: Loam holds just enough water and air and is rich in humus.

wrong.1: Pure sand dries out too fast and holds few nutrients.
wrong.2: Hard clay holds too much water when wet and bakes hard when dry.
